scope: Proposition 5.3 (Critical cutting and the exact contact rule) of the manuscript “The critical Liouville quantum sphere and geometric limits of FK maps at q=4” (preprints/The-critical-Liouville-quantum-sphere-and-geometric-limits-of-FK-maps-at-q-equals-4-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9b9236021eab20eb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 53. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider a critical field disk with a boundary-typical source and a target at any prescribed strictly interior relative boundary length. Its independent symmetric bSLE0,0 4 exploration admits a trunk-time parametrization in which the left and right boundary lengths have the law of Lemma 5.1. Conditional on the full length path, the jump interiors are independent critical disks with the corresponding perimeters and pinch marks. At the compact-surviving deterministic times and selected jump stops used below, the remaining disk has the marked disk law conditional on the observed past length data. The trunk is a simple continuous arc, all jump domains are Jordan domains, and two contour occurrences have the same physical image exactly when they satisfy the contact relation of Defini- tion 5.2. In particular no side class links two distinct real trunk times, no class identifies distinct points of one outer or jump circle, and no inserted positive circle visits the original boundary. The full exploration, including its ordered loop tours, is obtained as the limit of the subcritical cuttings on compact surviving pieces, with the terminal remainder shrinking spatially to the target.
